verdict.rationale: Working Copy documents SSH as a Git transport. Private keys can be imported or generated in the app, can live on the Secure Enclave, and can be used to reach regular Linux/BSD/NAS servers via SSH commands. However, the evidence never names the supported key algorithms, and the SSH use shown is Git-oriented rather than general server sessions. missing for 10: explicit documentation of Ed25519, ECDSA and RSA key support, evidence of general-purpose SSH connections to remote servers beyond Git operations, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can connect to remote servers using SSH with Ed25519, ECDSA, or RSA keys

citations.quote: Working Copy supports https, ssh, git, and http protocols.
For extra security SSH keys can reside on the Secure Enclave protected by Face ID or Touch ID.
You attach a private key to your Identity which can be imported or generated inside the app.
configure a regular Linux server, BSD server & Synology NAS to act as a hosting provider, using SSH commands for listing repositories.
